newsitem.title: USA: Holder urges Baldwin to explore sale.
newsitem.headline: Holder urges Baldwin to explore sale.

text.p: Kenneth Pavia Sr, general partner in Bolero Investment Group LP on Thursday urged Baldwin Piano & Organ Co's board to explore alternatives for enhancing shareholder value, including a possible merger.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Pavia said he was pleased Baldwin decided to hire the investment banking firm of Lehman Brothers to evaluate ways to enhance the company's value.
"It is now incumbent upon the board to work promptly and effectively with Lehman Brothers to develop and implement a strategy that will increase shareholder value," Pavia said.
According to the filing, Baldwin's board also amended its bylaws to make it more difficult for shareholders to nominate directors or bring other matters before an annual meeting.

Pavia said he was disappointed Baldwin would do this, "making it more difficult for shareholders to exercise their fundamental rights to nominate directors and bring other actions before meetings of their fellow shareholders."
The group has an 8.2 percent stake in Baldwin.
Baldwin, based in Loveland, Ohio, manufactures and distributes pianos, electronic organs, clocks, printed circuit boards and wooden cabinets.
